title: Quant profile validation watchtower with contextual golden cohorts
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build an automated validation 'watchtower' that runs quantization profile acceptance checks across FP8/INT8 variants using contextualized golden cohorts rather than a single monolithic golden set. The watchtower will: (1) select one or more golden cohorts for each model+workload slice (e.g., short-chat, long-instruction, search-rewrite), (2) run stochastic ensemble baselines and adversarial perturbation augmentations, (3) compute per-cohort pass/fail and a consolidated confidence score using layer-sensitivity envelopes, and (4) emit gate decisions that can be consumed by the quant rollouts pipeline and the canary release system.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Watchtower runs nightly on the quant CI cluster and produces a per-model JSON report in the artifacts bucket. 2) For each model variant (FP8/INT8), the report contains cohort-level metrics: BLEU/ROUGE-like custom similarity, semantic embedding drift (cosine delta), perplexity delta against ensemble baseline, and per-layer sensitivity score. 3) Pass/fail logic: cohort passes if all three primary metrics are within configured thresholds for that model and consolidated confidence >= 0.85. 4) A GitHub Action gate reads the report and blocks PR merges that would enable an auto-rollout unless a manual override label is present. 5) Coverage: at least 5 golden cohorts per model family and 200 unique prompts per cohort for initial rollout.
technical_design: Core components: (A) Cohort selector service that maps model, prompt-topic, and target latency bucket to a curated golden cohort. Cohorts are stored as versioned artifacts in S3 with metadata (seed, distribution stats, difficulty). (B) Orchestrator job (Kubernetes CronJob) that runs the quantized execution pipeline using the runtime staging cluster; it executes both deterministic replays and stochastic sampling with n=16 seeds for ensemble baselines. (C) Metrics engine that computes: embedding-cosine-delta (avg+95th), token-level perplexity delta, output edit-distance normalized for length, and layer-sensitivity envelope computed from per-layer KL divergence profiles. (D) Gate evaluator that applies configurable thresholds and produces an actionable decision plus human-readable rationale and a short diffsnapshot of failure examples. (E) Artifacts and telemetry: JSON reports in S3, Prometheus metrics for trend analysis, and a Kibana dashboard linked from Console.
metrics_and_thresholds:
- Embedding cosine delta (avg) <= 0.03; 95th percentile <= 0.08
- Perplexity delta <= 5% relative to FP32 baseline
- Normalized edit distance (NED) <= 0.04 for structured output cohorts, <= 0.08 for free-form chat cohorts
- Consolidated confidence score >= 0.85 computed as weighted sum: 0.4*embedding_score + 0.3*perplexity_score + 0.2*ned_score + 0.1*stability_score
- Layer-sensitivity envelope: no layer should exceed 2.5x baseline variance or flag for manual review
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for cohort selector and gate logic. 2) Integration test: run watchtower in a staging namespace with three models (llama-3-small, redwood-alpha-7B, open-7B) and seeded cohorts. 3) Adversarial smoke test: inject paraphrase/noise perturbations and confirm fail cases are detected. 4) Canary test: wire gate to a manual-only rollout for one dedicated capacity customer and observe manual override flow. 5) Performance: full nightly run time should be <= 3 hours for up to 10 models; target median latency per prompt under 1s on staging GPU pool.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): implement core orchestration and one-off reporter; run in dry-run mode and publish reports to S3. Phase 2 (week 3-4): integrate gate evaluator with CI (GitHub Actions) and add Prometheus metrics and dashboard. Phase 3 (week 5): enable automatic gate-based blocking for non-critical rollouts; manual override allowed with LABEL:quant-override. Phase 4 (post-release): expand cohorts to 10 models, tune thresholds based on historical runs, and add auto-labeling assistance in Console.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: false positives due to narrow cohort selection. Mitigation: require multiple cohort fails before blocking auto-rollout and maintain a 'context diversity' metric.
- Risk: nightly job exceeds billing/compute budget. Mitigation: cap stochastic samples per model and add sampling rate controls per-priority.
- Risk: metrics drift as new prompts introduced. Mitigation: rolling golden updates with curator sign-off and stable-seed replay capability.
- Risk: operator confusion from opaque gates. Mitigation: include human-readable rationale and example failure pairs in report and Console link.
open_decisions:
- Final weighting for consolidated confidence (current draft uses 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1) needs PM sign-off.
- Whether to treat structured-output cohorts (JSON/form schema) with stricter NED thresholds by default.
- Agree on retention policy for golden cohorts (current proposal: 90 days for active cohorts, archive thereafter).
- Decide if gate blocks should also record an audit action to the Private deployments audit log for enterprise customers.

notes: This ticket intentionally uses 'cohort' and 'watchtower' language to distinguish from previous 'golden-runner' projects. The goal is to provide a more contextual acceptance layer that meshes with model workload slices and reduces brittle single-golden failures. Work here will feed into the quant gatekeeper orchestration and Console QA pages.
